speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. You mentioned a limp and pain in a specific area; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what makes it worse? Also, how long has this been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain is referred to the left knee but there is no trauma, could you point to exactly where he hurts most if I pressed on his hip, thigh, or knee? Also, does he have any night pain that wakes him up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE)

Please perform the physical examination to check for limited internal rotation and abduction of the left hip, and perform the "chair test" to see if he can sit comfortably with both legs on the ground without pain. While you prepare for that, I am requesting an X-RAY: Left Pelvis AP and Frog-Leg lateral view.
